summary.headline: KFin Q1 FY27 revenue grew 30% YoY to consolidate Ascent (ex-Ascent ~10%), while PAT was flat-to-down and EBITDA margin fell to 34.2% with Ascent.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations rose 30% YoY, with about 9.6% growth excluding Ascent, and 2.7% QoQ including Ascent (1.6% excluding). EBITDA grew about 7.1% YoY, but consolidated EBITDA margin was 34.2% with Ascent versus 39.4% without it. PAT margin was 21% including Ascent and 26.6% excluding it, and PAT was broadly flat to marginally down YoY. Management raised its FY27 growth outlook to EBITDA growth of 17-20% and PAT growth of 12-15%, while a yield decline of about 2% QoQ in mutual funds was attributed to debt-to-liquid mix shift and provisioning for a pending large-client renewal.

financial_highlights.change: About INR 200 crore to go to dividend already declared

financial_highlights.value: About 51% of EBITDA converted to free cash flow

financial_highlights.change: from US$5.7 million in Q4; US$4.4 million in Q1 FY26 (pre-consolidation), +32% YoY

segments.name: Domestic mutual fund (RTA/fund admin)
segments.commentary: Industry AUM grew about 15% YoY versus KFin about 16%; KFin's equity AUM market share rose about 80 bps QoQ. Yield fell about 2% QoQ, of which about 30% was debt-to-liquid mix and the rest mainly provisioning for a pending large-client renewal.

segments.name: Issuer solutions
segments.commentary: Managed about 80% of main-board IPO issue size in Q1 and holds about 50% of NSE 500 market share (versus ~52% earlier). Corporate actions are about 30% of issuer revenue; the company guided to tepid corporate actions in Q2 due to IT services dividend deferrals.

segments.name: International (Ascent and global fund solutions)
segments.commentary: Revenue up about 200% YoY with Ascent and about 32% organically. Ascent EBITDA margin was about 8%; management targets double-digit margin within 12 months. Sequential decline ex-Ascent was attributed to pipeline timing, with growth expected above 25%.

segments.name: Alternatives (XAlt, GIFT City)
segments.commentary: About 731 funds with about 37.3% market share, targeting close to 40% with pending launches. 15 new AIF wins in Q1; the AIF business has compounded above 60% over four years and management expects at least 40% growth going forward.

segments.name: Pensions (NPS)
segments.commentary: Reached break-even last quarter and now contributes about 15%+ EBITDA margin. Manages about 2.5 million pensioners and is the second-largest CRA in India.

segments.name: Wealth management (mPower Wealth) and technology
segments.commentary: Three wealth platform mandates won. An INR 25 crore+ big-data mandate runs over about 18 months, with INR 40 crore of signed bolt-on deals across 3-15 month durations.

guidance_outlook: Revenue CAGR guided at 18-20%, unchanged from prior guidance.
Consolidated EBITDA margin guided at 40-45%; management aims to hold 40% threshold including Ascent by end of FY27.
FY27 visibility of EBITDA growth of about 17-20% and PAT growth of 12-15%, ahead of the earlier high-single to low-double-digit indication.
Ascent to become EBITDA accretive by end-FY27 or early FY28; double-digit margin targeted within the next 12 months; KFin-level EBITDA margin expansion to take three to five years.
Cost optimisation benefits expected from Q2 FY27 onwards; mutual fund yield expected to stabilise, with management unwilling to guide a yield number.
Target of at least 20% of revenue from controllable (non-market) businesses; currently about 6% from VAS plus 5-6% from other non-market businesses.
capex_capacity: Ascent cost base is being rationalised through shared support functions, consolidated office space and better vendor contracts (AWS, Oracle, Microsoft); contract renewals roll into KFin structures in October and January.

Mutual fund platform transformation under FinEx: SIP processing now completes within three working days for 99.7% of transactions (versus about 21 days industry); next launch by end-calendar 2026 to automate non-commercial and purchase transactions.
Cayman Islands facility being set up to meet regulatory substance requirements, a near-term cost already in the plan.
Infrastructure cost pressure (servers, routers, laptops) noted; management will be harder on client discount negotiations.
demand_pricing: Mutual fund yield fell about 2% QoQ: debt-to-liquid shift (debt yields 2-2.5x liquid) contributed about 30% of the decline, and provisioning for a large-contract renewal this year accounted for the rest. Management guides against a fixed yield number, citing asset-mix and AMC-growth effects.
Ascent revenue hit by digital-asset fund markdowns, offset by six new fund managers with over US$100 million each (transitions taking 3-5 months) and fund launches.

Retail participation is still weak, with Demat net additions slowing despite IPOs; IPO pipeline includes PhonePe, Zepto, Jio, Manipal Health and Razorpay, plus Razorpay, Garuda and Pushp Brand mandates won.
Management expects strong corporate actions outside IT services; IT services firms have deferred dividends, which could weigh on Q2.
Pending Philippines government contract: KFin is reported as highest bidder on technical and commercial scores, but no award has been announced.

qa_highlights.question: Karthik (Indus Capital): What cost takeouts drove better domestic MF segment margins despite single-digit revenue growth and yield compression, and can segment margins bottom out if yields stabilise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management credited technology-led cost optimisation across payroll, non-payroll and licensing, not ad-hoc cuts; full increments were given this year. It said yield is driven by pricing/discounts, asset mix and AMC growth, and that pricing-driven stability is expected from here, with the SIP automation and next FinEx launch (by end calendar 2026) as controllable margin levers.

qa_highlights.question: Karthik: how much of the PAT gap (about INR 47 million between INR 799 million and INR 752 million) narrows via cost takeouts versus revenue growth, and over what period?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is both, weighted more to top-line growth at Ascent (EBITDA about 7-8%), while KFin-level cost optimisation will do the heavy lifting. PAT pressure is largely non-cash amortisation of goodwill/contract payments and capitalised One Constellation platform costs.

qa_highlights.question: Swarnab Mukherjee (360 ONE): Is the yield drop only debt-to-liquid mix, how should yield be modelled over the remaining three quarters given ~2% QoQ fall, and how will bolt-on wins add revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said equity mix was stable and the shift was debt to liquid (debt yields 2-2.5x liquid), plus provisioning for a large renewal this year. It declined to guide a yield number, saying conservatism means sticking to about 3% annual decline, though a reversal could give an upside surprise. Bolt-on deals of about INR 40 crore signed in Q1 run for 3, 6 and 15 months and are episodic, not annuity.

qa_highlights.question: Swarnab: why did international ex-Ascent revenue fall QoQ, and how should it be modelled?
qa_highlights.answer: Vivek Mathur said the decline reflects contracts in the pipeline that will materialise in coming quarters, not a fundamental change. He expects growth above 25% and called it a one-quarter phenomenon.

qa_highlights.question: Arjun Bagga (DSP MF): what is the split of the yield decline between debt-to-liquid mix and renegotiation provisions, and will Ascent margins reach double digits next quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: About 30% of the 2% yield decline came from debt-to-liquid; the remaining ~1.7% was net of asset-class moves, mainly provisioning for pending renegotiation, partly offset by ETF-to-equity movement. Double-digit Ascent margin is targeted within the next 12 months, not next quarter; the QoQ fall reflected crypto fund markdowns offset by new wins and fund launches. On discounts, management said it will be harder on client discount negotiations given infrastructure cost pressure.

qa_highlights.question: Abhijeet (Kotak): number of Ascent $100m+ clients, whether the wins are new or transitions, Ascent AUM vs revenue mix, deal size and FY guidance.
qa_highlights.answer: Six new fund managers with over $100 million each were won; these are transitions from incumbents, taking 3-5 months. The INR 25 crore data mandate is a single client with two contracts over about 18 months, milestone-based. Management gave FY27 visibility of EBITDA growth of 17-20% and PAT growth of 12-15%, ahead of the earlier high-single to low-double-digit indication. It did not give a digital-asset revenue split.

qa_highlights.question: Madhukar (JP Morgan): Ascent dollar revenue QoQ and yield, and Southeast Asia (GFS) yield.
qa_highlights.answer: Ascent revenue rose from US$5.7 million in Q4 to US$5.9 million, +32% YoY against US$4.4 million in Q1 FY26 pre-consolidation. Vivek said the Southeast Asia margin improved on AUM growth there and hoped it would be sustained, without confirming the 5.3 bps yield.

qa_highlights.question: Prayesh Jain (Motilal Oswal): Philippines contract timing and profitability, issuer-solutions growth versus company growth, segment profitability, and wealth management economics.
qa_highlights.answer: No Philippines win has been announced; KFin is reported as highest bidder on technical and commercial scores, and the client has not awarded the contract. Corporate actions are about 30% of issuer revenue, and retail participation remains weak. Wealth pricing has two models: fixed platform-implementation fees (20-35% of contract value) and basis points on AUM. Segment profitability was referred to IR.

risks_watch: Mutual fund yield: about 2% QoQ fall in Q1 with about 1.7% left after the debt-to-liquid effect; further renegotiation provisions for a large renewal this year; no yield number guided.
Corporate actions in issuer solutions (about 30% of issuer revenue) guided tepid for Q2 as top-tier IT services firms defer dividends; retail participation and Demat net additions are slowing.
Ascent margins: about 8% EBITDA, with double-digit targeted within 12 months; crypto fund markdowns weigh on AUM and revenue; consolidated margin is 34.2% including Ascent versus 39.4% without.
Cost-optimisation benefits are guided from Q2 FY27, and the PAT gap is driven by non-cash amortisation and capitalised platform costs. Watch for PAT growth converting to the guided 12-15%.

Philippines government contract remains unawarded; bolt-on tech deal revenue (about INR 40 crore signed) is lumpy and phased over 3-15 months; the Cayman Islands substance facility adds near-term cost.
key_quotes: Excluding Ascent also, we have grown nearly 10% thereabouts, EBITDA grew about 7% plus and the PAT, there was a marginal decline to flattish performance, largely on account of the depreciation amortization and several non-cash items

So, we have moved a couple of notches from there. And whilst, as you know, we do not necessarily give formal guidance, we have visibility for EBITDA growth closer to 20 %, anywhere between 17% to 20%, and our PAT numbers anywhere between 12% to 15%.
I would even guide to slightly tepid corporate action movement into at least the next quarter, as you may have seen that several top-tier IT services companies have decided not to declare dividends
No, we have not announced any win. I mean, there was a media leak in terms of us being identified as the highest bidder in terms of both technical and commercials.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on growth, the FY27 EBITDA (17-20%) and PAT (12-15%) outlook, and the international pipeline, but cautious on mutual fund yield, which it declined to quantify, and on Q2 corporate actions. It was evasive on the Philippines award and segment-level profitability, referring those to IR.
